hero: At a table on a Quezon City hospital ward, a Filipina nephrology fellow and a resident sit with a 58-year-old Filipino man with a tunneled neck dialysis catheter dressing and his adult daughter, sorting a folder of printed laboratory results and forms, while the man's son appears on a phone video call propped against a water bottle; afternoon light, calm and practical mood, no text.

figures.teaches: PhilHealth kidney benefits (HD, PD and transplant) all start from a true diagnosis of chronic kidney disease stage 5 and PDD registration, and none of them should set the prescription.
figures.content: Top box: 'Chronic kidney disease stage 5, with evidence of chronicity' arrow to 'PDD registration (before the first claimed session)'. Three branches below. Branch 1 'Hemodialysis': 'Up to 156 sessions per calendar year', 'PHP 6,350 per session (from October 9, 2024, per PhilHealth 2025 release)', 'Up to PHP 990,600 per year', 'Includes facility and professional fees', 'Unused sessions do not carry over'. Branch 2 'Peritoneal dialysis Z benefit (PC 2024-0036)': 'Adults: CAPD', 'Children: CAPD and APD', 'Contracted PD providers', 'Follow the treatment plan; do not share or sell solutions'. Branch 3 'Kidney transplant Z benefit (Revision 1, PC 2026-0019)': 'Adults and children; living or deceased donor', 'Contracted centers only; pre-authorization valid 180 days', 'Package rates PHP 865,000 to 2,146,000 by donor type, induction and surgery', 'No copayment in ward; no balance billing for covered services', 'Return to HD or PD benefit if the graft fails'. Bottom banner: 'Services follow clinical assessment, not demand. Confirm rates on the date of service.'

figures.teaches: A safe dialysis transfer carries ten items and ends with a call and a confirmed first session.
figures.content: Clipboard checklist with ten tick boxes: 1 'Diagnosis, cause, chronicity, date of first dialysis'. 2 'PDD status and sessions used this year'. 3 'Current prescription as written by the attending'. 4 'Access type, site, date; permanent access plan'. 5 'HBsAg, anti-HCV, HIV with dates; hepatitis B vaccination'. 6 'Recent labs with dates; pending results and who follows them'. 7 'Medicines: what changed and why; allergies'. 8 'Residual urine; heart, volume, BP; events in the chair'. 9 'Goals of care and decision-makers'. 10 'Sending attending name and number'. Below, three icons in a row: 'Copy to the patient', 'Physician-to-physician call', 'First session date confirmed'.
